Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: issue "processing report and doc removal" (local ID `processing-report-and-doc-removal`, Refs #8723)

**Planning ref:** `orchestrator/project-8723` @ `9faaab9b587ea16ff647a0892e67ba45142ff2ee` (integration branch mismatch: false). I compared it against `isolated-base`, the default branch as it was when this run started.

**One item needs a decision at implement time.** On this ref the memory retry-reason telemetry is only partly there. Its tests, changelog and agents fragment are present, but the code in `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py` and `scripts/ai_memory.py` is unchanged. The plan marks that item `rejected` unless the implementer's checkout shows otherwise (D2).

## Files likely to change
- `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-30.md` (delete)
- `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (append one entry at the end)
- `tests/test_apply_analysis_on_main.py` (check only; no edit expected)

## Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- No new script and no new supervisor. Only the data/doc file changes.
- Scheduler entry point: none needed. The existing `scripts/apply_analysis_on_main.sh` already uses this report. Its candidate scan (line 341) skips any doc whose file name appears in `APPLY_ANALYSIS_REPORT_PATH` (default `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`). Its prompt (line 500) sets the rule this issue follows: delete the source doc and append one entry.
- No database work, and no new entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends the existing per-source-doc entry format of `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (the `### \`analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-29.md\`` entry at line 1746)
Scope-mode justification: The issue spells out the whole deliverable: delete one doc and append one report entry, with the verdicts already decided. No code change is needed. The entry reuses the existing heading and metadata lines (`Source doc:`, `Processed:`, `Source commit:`) and adds the per-recommendation verdict table the issue asks for. The only judgement left is the check, required by the issue, that each `applied` sibling really landed. I did that check here (see the evidence table), and the implementer re-runs the one check that can change the result (D2). Doing the complete version costs no more than a shortcut, so nothing is left out; completeness serves correctness (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed).

## Functions or modules to implement
None. The work is data and docs only:
1. Delete `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-30.md` with `git rm`.
2. Append to `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`. The file currently ends with `- DEAD-API: no findings.\n`, so write one blank line and then the new entry. Do not change any byte of the earlier text, including the `## Processed source docs (128)` list, its count, and the 2026-09-29 entry. Use this layout:

```
### `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-30.md`
Source doc: `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-30.md`
Processed: <date -u +%F at implement time; expected 2026-11-03>
Source commit: `fcb44ee4855705d0d63231dd1c6a66ba51b293e4`

| Recommendation | Verdict | Evidence / reason |
|---|---|---|
...rows below...
```

Table rows to transcribe. Escape any literal `|` inside a cell as `\|`, for example in `status=ready\|timeout\|api_error`.

**Applied**
- **Speed 1 / Reliability 3 / GH API audit row 1** (pending check identities and wait exit reason): applied. Each poll in `scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py` emits `CHECK_RUNS_WAIT_PENDING`, and the wait ends with `CHECK_RUNS_WAIT_EXIT` (`status=ready|timeout|api_error`). Pinned by `tests/test_collect_pr_check_runs_pending_identity.py`; changelog `changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-30-check-run-pending-identity.md` (Refs #8724).
- **Speed 2, logging half:** applied. The `codex-agent` job in `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` has a `Show disk usage (pre free-disk-space)` step before `Free disk space`. Both the pre and post steps log `df -B1 --output=avail,size /`. Pinned by `tests/test_review_autofix_disk_headroom_contract.py`; changelog `changelog.d/8725-review-disk-headroom-logging.md`.
- **AI Memory Health** (push retry-reason telemetry): conditional, see D2. On this ref it is **rejected**. Reason: the sibling for #8726 landed only `tests/test_ai_memory_push_retry_reasons.py`, the `tests/test_ai_memory_cli.py` assertions, `changelog.d/8726-memory-push-retry-reasons.md` and `agents.d/8726-memory-push-retry-reasons.md`. `persist_memory_operation` in `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py` and the telemetry in `scripts/ai_memory.py` are identical to the default branch. There is no `push_retry_reasons`, `_classify_memory_push_retry_reason` or `_MEMORY_PUSH_RETRY_REASONS_MAX`, so the telemetry is not emitted.
- **DUP-002:** applied. `emit_reviewer_common_context_sections()` in `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` is called by both the full and the scoped reviewer prompt builders. Pinned by `tests/test_review_reviewer_common_context_sections.py`; changelog `changelog.d/8738-reviewer-common-context-sections.md`.
- **CONSIST-001:** applied. The local `gh_retry()` wrapper is gone from `scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh`, and its callers now use `gh_retry_to_file <file> gh ...` directly. No changelog fragment exists, and the PR number cannot be recovered from this branch's squashed history.

**Already implemented**
- **Cost 1 / Reliability 1:** `_dedupe_structured_cost_telemetry_full_logs` and `_strip_structured_cost_telemetry_key_timestamp` in `scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py`.
- **SEC-001:** all 4 `actions/checkout` steps in `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml` set `persist-credentials: false`.
- **SEC-002:** `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` logs through `_gh_cmd_log_summary` plus the escaped `_gh_final_stderr_excerpt`.
- **BUG-001:** all 5 executable `gh pr merge` calls in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` pass `--match-head-commit`. One of them passes it through `_rb_mwf_match_arg`.
- **BUG-002:** `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` requires `state=open` and an exact head-repo match.
- **API-003:** HTTP 401 / `Bad credentials` is handled in `_is_gh_permanent_failure`.
- **API-004:** `gh_retry` makes a single attempt for a non-idempotent create.
- **EXPR-001:** the `Stage workflow support files` step in `.github/workflows/implement.yml` passes values through `STAGE_*` `env:` variables.
- **Speed 4 / Cost 5** (pre-submission parity): the pre-push affected-test gate exists (agents.md, "Pre-push affected-test gate").
- **GH API request-count telemetry:** `GH_API_RETRY` lines in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`.

**Rejected** (one row each, with the issue's reasons copied as written)
- Reliability 2 inventory entry for `scripts/guard_differential.py`: obsolete; the file does not exist on main, and the failure was branch-local.
- Speed 1 overlap of polling with cleanup, and the Speed 2 conditional skip: they need the new measurements first, and they put the merge gate and disk at risk.
- Speed 3 / Cost 3: high quality risk and no defined spec.
- Cost 2 / Cost 4: open-ended, with no verified duplication.
- Reliability 4 / Orchestrator Health / Pipeline Flow: open-ended instrumentation without concrete evidence or a spec.
- Memory retrieve truncation logging: only needed if the budget is enlarged, which is not planned.
- API-001, API-002, BATCH-001, BATCH-002, API-005, MERGE-001: tagged RISKY_SKIP by the doc itself.
- DUP-001: label contract parity is already covered by `tests/test_ai_label_precreation_contract.py`, and the change would touch the hot poller.
- DUP-003: `tests/test_workflow_gh_retry_fallback_contract.py` deliberately requires the local fallbacks for older support refs.
- DEAD-001: a no-op cleanup in the hot poller; not worth the conflict risk.
- SHELL-001: style-only (§9).
- DEBT-001: `tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py` enforces the 480,000-byte guard; extraction is only required once that guard is reached (§24).

**Informational rows**
- REUSE and DEAD-API: no findings (doc section "API Call Consolidation & Dead-Call Analysis").
- Prompt Cache & Memory System fingerprint: covered by the Cost 2 rejection.
- Per-Repo Breakdown top three actions: covered by the rows above (Cost 1, Speed 1/2, Reliability 2).

## Data structures affected
- Markdown only: one new `###` entry with a table at the end of the report, and one deleted doc.
- No schema, JSON or state files change. `analysis/last_collection_timestamp.txt`, `analysis/validation-selftest-status.json` and every other file under `analysis/` must not be touched.

## API or interface changes
None. The report keeps working with `apply_analysis_on_main.sh`: its `grep -qF <basename>` skip check finds `workflow-optimization-2026-09-30.md` in the new entry.

## Decisions
### D1 — Verdict layout
- Chosen: a markdown table (Recommendation | Verdict | Evidence / reason) under the usual `###` heading with `Source doc:`, `Processed:` and `Source commit:` lines.
- Alternatives considered: the bullet style used by the 2026-09-28-3 and 2026-09-29 entries.
- Why: the issue explicitly asks for a "per-recommendation verdict table". The metadata lines stay the same as earlier entries for consistency.

### D2 — The memory retry-reason item depends on what is actually on the branch
- Chosen: at implement time, run `grep -n 'push_retry_reasons\|_classify_memory_push_retry_reason' scripts/ai_memory_lib.py scripts/ai_memory.py`.
  - If there are hits in both files: mark the item `applied` and cite `changelog.d/8726-memory-push-retry-reasons.md`.
  - If there are none (as on this ref): mark it `rejected` with the reason given in the table above.
- Alternatives considered: mark it `applied` because a changelog entry exists; or implement the missing code here.
- Why: the issue requires confirming that each `applied` item merged, and says to reject any that did not. Implementing the code here would go outside files_t
